modern: You have endured endless troubles through not being content with your ruling faculty when it does the things which it is made by nature to do. But enough of this.
original: Thou hast endured infinite troubles through not being contented with thy ruling faculty when it does the things which it is constituted by nature to do. But enough [of this].
notification: You have endured endless troubles through not being content with your ruling faculty when it does the things which it is made by nature to do. But enough of this.
notification_original: Thou hast endured infinite troubles through not being contented with thy ruling faculty when it does the things which it is constituted by nature to do. But enough [of this].

explained.summary: You’ve put yourself through endless trouble by not being content to let your mind simply do its proper job. Marcus is telling himself that the problems came from wanting more than reason could give, and then he cuts himself off: enough of that.
